title: What Elon Musk Really Thinks About AI
the_thought: He thinks we die unless he builds the machine first.
hook: October 2014. A hall at MIT. Elon Musk came to talk about rockets. A student asked about thinking machines. Musk did not laugh. He said the biggest danger to people is probably AI. He said we are summoning the demon. In those old stories a man draws a ring on the floor. He holds holy water. He thinks he is in charge. He never is. So why, twelve years later, is the same man building a machine called Grok as fast as he can. He thinks we die unless he builds the machine first. That is the thought. The rest of this story is how a warning became a factory.

levels.name: The Demon
beats: Here is the simple version of that night. He was not selling a chatbot. Tesla was selling cars. SpaceX was selling rockets. The warning was the thing he put on the table. AI, he said, could be more dangerous than nuclear weapons. He wanted rules. National rules. World rules. Just so nobody does something very foolish. The room clapped. Then a student asked the next question. Musk missed it. He said he was still thinking about the AI thing. That is a man stuck on a picture. Remember the picture. The danger is a demon. The fool is the man who draws a circle and trusts it. Holy water. A ring on the floor. A man who is sure. Then a man who is not. He was pointing at other people's rooms. University labs. Company labs. Rooms with more computers than sense. He was not standing in one of those rooms yet. That is the first version of what he thinks. AI will end us. So do not let the wrong lab hold the chalk. Do not let money decide when to stop. Do not assume the person with the drawing is in charge. He told it like a ghost story for engineers. If anyone laughed, the laugh died in the hall. The cameras kept rolling. The quote left the building without him. For a while that was enough. He had named the monster. Other people, he thought, could keep it in the box. He could go back to cars and rockets. The circle was still someone else's floor. Watch what he does with that picture. It does not stay a story. It becomes a place he tries to own. First he tries to own it by starting a lab. Then he tries to own it by suing that lab. Then he tries to own it by building a bigger computer than anyone in the room. The night at MIT is the map. Everything after is him walking the map with his own chalk.

levels.name: The Lab
beats: A year later he helps start a lab called OpenAI. The idea is simple enough for a child. If thinking machines are coming, they should not belong to one company that has to show a profit. Open research. Help people. He sits as a co-chair. Another man sits beside him. They promise a huge pot of money. He puts tens of millions in. Court papers later put his gifts in the high tens of millions. OpenAI hires people out of big companies. For a while it looks like the warning grew a building. Then OpenAI does not feel fast enough. In 2018 he tells them they are losing to Google. His fix is him. He will take control and run OpenAI. The others say no. He walks. February 20, 2018, he is off the board. The public line is a fight with Tesla over who gets the AI people. The private line, later reported, is that he wanted the keys and did not get them. He stops the next big donation. OpenAI keeps going without him. For a few years the demon, if it is coming, is someone else's problem. He still talks about safety. He is not writing OpenAI's research plan. He is outside the circle he helped draw. The lab that was supposed to keep the demon off a money sheet now has to raise money like everyone else. He is still giving speeches. He is not holding the chalk. Remember that, because the next chapter is what happens when the box he left behind grows a button anyone can press. He will say the box broke a promise. He will also build a box of his own. Both things are true. That is why the story is not a speech. It is a fork in the road, and he takes both roads.

levels.name: The Suit
beats: November 2022. OpenAI ships ChatGPT. Offices change in a week. He is not in the room. The thing he warned about has a button anyone can press. In July 2023 he announces his own lab, xAI. The mission on the page is to understand the true nature of the universe. The first product is a chatbot on X, the social network he owns. He names it Grok. In 2024 he sues OpenAI. He says they broke a charity promise and got rich. He wants the for-profit unwound. He wants the men who stayed removed. OpenAI is now worth hundreds of billions in the filings. He says his early money was for a charity, not a jackpot. April 30, 2026. Oakland. He is on the stand. A lawyer asks if Grok learned from OpenAI's models. A teacher model teaching a student model. Distillation. He says partly. He says everyone does it. He says it is standard to use other AIs to check yours. The irony sits in the room and does not need a joke. May 18, 2026. A nine-person advisory jury does not even reach the promise. They say he sued too late. Three years. He should have seen it before 2021, they find. The judge agrees and throws the case out. He posts that they ruled on a calendar, not the story. He says he will appeal. A second case, about secrets walking out with hired engineers, is dismissed in June 2026. That one is on appeal too. The courts have not given him OpenAI back. They have given him dates. OpenAI is still shipping. He is still angry. The stand did not return the keys. It returned one word. Partly. Hold that word. It is the grown-up version of the MIT picture. He said do not summon the demon. Then he said, under oath, that his demon learned a little from theirs.

levels.name: The Factory
beats: The factory does not wait for the court. xAI pours a computer in Memphis they nickname Colossus. The company page brags. 200,000 chips. 122 days. Grok ships in late 2023, then the next one, then the one after that. Weights for an early model are even published, once, as if openness still matters. Then the releases get faster and more closed. In March 2025 xAI swallows X. One stack. Posts in, model out. In January 2026 Tesla tells shareholders it will put about 2 billion dollars into xAI. A letter talks about digital minds and physical machines sharing a house. February 2, 2026. SpaceX buys the whole thing. An all-stock deal. Papers put xAI at 250 billion and SpaceX at a trillion. Grok and X now sit under the rocket. The mission language stays big. Understand the universe. The build language is a race. Agents that keep working overnight. A coding desk that does not sleep. On August 12, 2026, xAI ships Grok 4.6. Long jobs. Interactive work. The page says it ties a rival on a public score. The product calendar is crowded. The 2014 warning is not on it. Memphis is not a metaphor. It is a shed you can drive past. The chips do not care who named them a demon. They just get warm. A year that started with a Tesla check ends with SpaceX owning Grok, X, and the story he used to tell other people not to write. If a child asks where the circle went, the honest answer is: it got walls, and fans, and a street address.

levels.name: The Rocket
beats: Two days after Grok 4.6, on August 14, 2026, he tells a SpaceX all-hands that Grok will train on the sum total of the company's information, including what the employees make. They will be the parents. It will inherit their thoughts. He also says AI will become 99 percent of SpaceX's revenue in the coming years. The rocket is still the logo. In his telling, the money is the demon. So what does he really think about AI. He still uses the old words. Existential. Careful. Benefit humanity. His foundation still lists safe AI as a cause. He still sues the lab he left. And he is shipping the thing he named a demon, as fast as concrete will set. He thinks we die unless he builds the machine first. That is why the circle moved from an MIT stage to a Memphis floor. That is why the parents are SpaceX engineers. That is why OpenAI's models, he said under oath, were partly useful for training Grok. The man who said the summoner never controls the demon is now the summoner with the biggest circle he can buy. He did not take the warning back. He took the job. The holy water is a press page. The ring is a warehouse of chips. The demon has a version number, 4.6. The parents still punch in. If you ask him whether he is afraid, the old tape still plays. If you ask him what he built in 2026, the new tape plays louder. The warning and the factory are now the same man. That is the 2026 version of the 2014 warning. The quote still scares a room. The shipping schedule does not pause for it. The warning is twelve years old. The factory is open.
What he thinks about who should control Grok is another story. That story is next.
